name: Bad bots
note: Subset fetched on 2026-10-18. The ai.robots.txt robots.txt had 188 user-agent tokens. The nginx bad-bot user-agent list had 700 lines. Credential stuffing is included as a pattern because those tools imitate a browser. Sample of the public lists, not the full lists.

entries.name: GPTBot
entries.meaning: GPTBot is a user-agent token on the public ai.robots.txt disallow list. Site owners use that list when they do not want this crawler fetching pages. A matching user agent is a signal, not proof of abuse.

block.note: On your own site, add the robots.txt lines and, if you use Cloudflare, a custom WAF rule with the expression above and the action Block.

entries.name: Credential stuffing
entries.pattern: Often a normal browser user agent. There is no single string to block.
entries.meaning: Credential stuffing reuses stolen passwords and usually pretends to be a normal browser. NCSC recommends a strong separate email password and 2-step verification, which cuts off the accounts these attacks target. This is a pattern, not a copied user-agent string.

block.robots: A robots.txt block does not stop credential stuffing.
block.cloudflare: On your own zone, rate-limit the sign-in path and challenge repeated failures. Pair that with 2-step verification on the accounts.
block.note: Do not put a seed phrase, password, or customer list in a block rule.
